newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia 93/94 energy use up 36 pct on 82/83.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia 93/94 energy use up 36 pct on 82/83.

text.p: Australia's energy consumption, including industrial, commercial and residential use, rose 36 percent to 2,853.5 petajoules in 1993/94 from 2,093.4 petajoules in 1982/83, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Monday.

Mining recorded the greatest increase in energy consumption for the period, with a rise of 160 percent to 196.1 petajoules from 75.3 petajoules, the bureau said in its Energy Accounts for Australia publication. Road transport -- the dominant sector in energy consumption -- rose 31 percent to 849.9 petajoules from 646.3 petajoules over the same period, it said.
Energy production increased 34 percent to 9,035.7 petajoules from 6,730.2 petajoules in the same period and energy exports nearly doubled to 6,414.1 petajoules from 3,884.2 petajoules.
A petajoule is a million billion joules.

In 1993/94 crude oil was the main source of domestic energy, accounting for 36 percent, followed by black coal at 29 percent, natural gas at 18 percent, brown coal at 12 percent, wood at five percent and solar at less than 0.1 percent, it said. As a proportion of world reserves, Australia accounts for about 0.3 percent of crude oil, 1.8 percent of natural gas, eight percent of black coal and 15 percent of brown coal, it said.
